---
title: "Fig 1; what to include?"
format: html
---


The current figure has a separate plot for studydesign, muscle volume, muscle thickness, arm lean mass, all the strength measures, and exercise data (total volume). While it is informative, I would like to try a simplified approach with one measure called "muscle mass" (or something along those lines) in one plot, one measure called "muscle strength" in on plot. The exercise data could be expressed as volume per session/age group/condition. So roughly:

- Panel A: Studydesign
- Panel B: Muscle Mass/Size
- Panel C: Muscle Strength
- Panel D: Training Volume

It's not obvious to me what the best approach would be to decide how to gather muscle volume and thickness under one, and the same for all of the strength measures. I think separating upper and lower body makes sense in all instances, since the data looks a bit different. The different measures could be combined using Z-score or percentage change:

Arguments from Claude discussion: 
- My four lower body strength measures (isometric, isok60, isok120, isok240, 1RM leg press) are all in different units/magnitudes — e.g. isometric peak torque might be ~200 Nm while isok240 might be ~100 Nm. If you just average them raw, the higher-magnitude measures dominate.
- Z-scoring rescales each measure to "how many SDs from baseline" — so all four contribute equally regardless of their original scale. You'd compute mean and SD at pre for each measure, then express all timepoints relative to that. The composite y-axis then reads as something like "standardized strength (SD units)."
- Percent change from pre is more intuitive ("strength increased by X%") but can be misleading if the measures have different % change sensitivities.
- For an overview figure, z-scoring is cleaner — the composite line just shows the overall trajectory, and the absolute numbers don't matter since you'll report those separately.
